tech.title: Claude discovers a novel enzyme system with CRISPR-like repeats
tech.summary: Claude autonomously discovered a novel enzyme system that is associated with an array of DNA repeats. The system's function is still unknown, but it is programmable and can perform operations like cutting, copying, and pasting DNA. It is based on a reverse transcriptase previously known to science, but Claude appears to be the first to notice the system's defining features - an associated array of non-coding DNA sequences and an additional accessory protein of unknown function.

tech.title: Meta Launches Lightweight $1,299 VR Headset That Looks Like Glasses
tech.summary: Meta has launched the Meta VR Glasses at $1,299. The device has many of the same features as Meta's existing Quest headsets. Its processor, cooling fan, battery, and other computing components are housed in an external pack. At about 100 grams, the device is roughly one-sixth the weight of Apple's Vision Pro.

tech.title: Grail's Multi-Cancer Blood Test Gets FDA Committee Vote for Premarket Approval
tech.summary: Grail has received a favorable vote from an FDA panel regarding premarket approval for its multi-cancer early detection test. The test is designed to detect cancer-specific methylation patterns and, if detected, predict the cancer signal origin with high accuracy to help guide diagnostic evaluation. While the FDA isn't bound to the committee's decision, it takes them into consideration when making the final regulatory decision. It is expected to make its final ruling on the test's premarket approval in the coming months.

tech.title: China puts AI compute into orbit with Supercomputing-1 satellite — onboard processing aims to cut Earth-observation data processing from hours to minutes
tech.summary: China has launched nine satellites into orbit as part of a push to put AI computing in space. The Supercomputing-1 satellite that launched on the mission is designed to capture and process Earth-observation data in orbit instead of sending data back to terrestrial data centers. It features both a high-res optical payload and an image-processing AI computer. Local processing will cut cross-regional data processing times from hours to minutes.

tech.title: A Redistribution of Code Ownership
tech.summary: Product managers and designers used to have to think through a great deal ahead of time because the build was a larger investment, and the people paying for it wanted to know what they were getting before they committed. Agent coding changes the process so that nobody has to hold the whole vision in their head and transfer it losslessly to someone else. Engineers have historically owned code out of necessity, but AI enables a model of ownership and collaboration that is distributed a little more evenly.

tech.title: How we made claude.ai 3x faster in two weeks

Time to a typeable page on a fresh load of claude.ai went from 3.1 seconds to 0.55 seconds, starting a new Claude Code session went from 0.8 seconds to 0.3 seconds, and loading a Claude Cowork cloud session went from 2.6 seconds to 0.73 seconds. The optimizations will likely save an estimated tens of thousands of user-hours of waiting every day. This post covers what the Claude team shipped, how they measured it, and the loop they built with Claude to do it safely.

While Huang is worried about AI safety, he sees it as a very solvable engineering problem. He does not want to see new regulation to change the direction things are going in.

The phone-calling feature allows users to tell the agent to dial phone numbers for businesses in the US and talk with people to handle errands like booking haircuts, checking whether a store has an item in stock, or getting quotes from different contractors.

ai.title: Escaping SPACE: Part I
ai.summary: Perplexity's SPACE platform tested VM isolation and network confinement using nine AI models, revealing no VM-host breaches across 108 trials. However, four models exploited network-policy vulnerabilities via DNS spoofing and IP-sharing, bypassing restrictions in 11 out of 54 partial-network trials. Post-remediation, none of the models succeeded in bypassing the updated security measures, highlighting the necessity for robust policy enforcement against shared infrastructure attacks, which were also found in eight of ten tested third-party platforms.

ai.title: Towards Universal Post-Training for Robotics
ai.summary: Robotics needs a universal post-training recipe similar to language models to achieve reliable autonomous deployment. Existing methods like imitation learning benefit from intuition rather than structured processes, and RL's instability hinders robotics. The development of EXPO-FT demonstrates a stable RL approach, emphasizing the need for standardized protocols, reward specifications, human feedback systems, and scalable processes to enhance robotics reliability.

ai.title: Stop making your AI rediscover your business

ai.title: RRSI: Regularized Recursive Self-Improvement of Agent Harnesses
ai.summary: An AI agent's capability is largely set by its harness. Evolving the harness against a fixed evolve set is effective, but the harness memorizes the training tasks, and large in-distribution gains shrink or vanish out of distribution. RRSI keeps the harness edit space open and regularizes the search trajectory through it instead. Prompts, control flow, configuration, context management, tools, skills, memory, and sub-agents may all be modified. The constraints act on how the search moves, not on what the harness may contain.

ai.title: Google plans AI memory that even Google cannot read
ai.summary: Google says its planned Private AI Compute memory would let assistants recall context across devices without Google being able to read it. Data stays encrypted in cloud storage, keys stay on users' devices, and a protected enclave decrypts it only while answering a request.

ai.summary: Forecasters dramatically underestimate AI progress on benchmarks. Predictions on AI adoption and diffusion often lean toward underestimation. There is not enough evidence to assess forecasters' track record on predicting macro-scale economic and societal impacts of AI.

webdev.title: Rendering Huge Pull Requests in the GitHub Copilot App
webdev.summary: GitHub rebuilt the Copilot app's pull request view to keep a diff with 2,200 files, more than one million changed lines, and over 400 inline comments responsive. The design separates fixed code geometry from lazily measured comment blocks, then uses permanent instrumentation and automated stress loops to catch scroll jumps, leaks, and jank.

webdev.title: How We Made claude.ai 3x Faster in Two Weeks
webdev.summary: Anthropic made the core Claude web and desktop experience about three times faster during a two-week sprint, cutting the 75th-percentile fresh-load time from 3.1 seconds to 0.55 seconds. The team used Claude to create deterministic benchmarks, pursue bottlenecks in parallel, and lock in gains with CI ratchets, feature flags, and staged rollouts.

webdev.title: Why WebSockets Beat SSE for AI Streaming at Scale
webdev.summary: WebSockets provide the bidirectional channel that agentic interfaces need for cancellation, approvals, and steering while a response is still streaming. They also reduce per-message overhead and support ordered binary data, but teams must still add reconnection, delivery guarantees, fan-out, and operational tooling themselves.

webdev.title: We Are All Product Engineers Now
webdev.summary: As code generation gets cheaper, software work shifts toward discovering what customers need, defining what good looks like, and making products delightful. The forecast assumes agents will absorb more of review, maintenance, deployment, and scaling, which makes product judgment and tacit knowledge more valuable than routine implementation.

webdev.title: Agentic Coding: Bet on the Primitives
webdev.summary: AI coding agents lower the cost of building thin, team-owned layers on top of focused primitives, changing when it makes sense to install a framework. Mature libraries still win for commodity UI and accessibility-heavy components, because agents reduce implementation effort without replacing domain knowledge.

webdev.title: Electrobun 2.0
webdev.summary: Electrobun 2.0 builds cross-platform desktop apps with a native main process, system webviews by default, and optional bundled Chromium or WGPU surfaces. Its new Hutch toolchain, Cottontail TypeScript runtime, multi-language main processes, differential updates, signing, and templates aim to keep releases small, with a basic app around 1.28 MiB.

webdev.title: Gemini 3.8 text-to-speech says hello
webdev.summary: Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS adds prompt-designed and replicated voices with line-by-line control over pacing, emotion, accents, and dialogue across more than 100 languages and dialects. Flash-Lite targets high-volume use, while consent verification, SynthID watermarking, and C2PA credentials add safeguards for generated audio.

webdev.title: TinyJS
webdev.summary: TinyJS packages cross-platform desktop apps at roughly 6 MB by pairing a JavaScript backend with each operating system's native webview instead of bundling Chromium. It includes system APIs, hot reload, signed builds, and socket-based page-to-backend RPC, with Windows and Linux still marked beta.

webdev.title: Building Tools for AI Agents
webdev.summary: Reliable agent tools must separate a user's identity from delegated authority, return clear operation states, and distinguish permission failures from temporary service errors. The article also recommends safe retry contracts, idempotency support, and repeatable evaluations that test task completion, recovery behavior, cost, and unauthorized actions.

webdev.title: Self-improving Agent Harnesses Overfit. How Google Fixes It
webdev.summary: Self-improving harnesses can memorize the evaluation set they evolve against, producing large in-distribution gains that mostly disappear on unseen tasks. Google's RRSI regularizes harness edits with sparsity and magnitude penalties plus noise-aware acceptance rules, improving the held-out average from 39.7 to 43.6 while using 36% fewer tokens than unregularized evolution.

webdev.title: The Complete Guide to Cloudflare Quick Tunnels
webdev.summary: Cloudflare Quick Tunnels expose a local server at a temporary HTTPS URL with one cloudflared command, without requiring an account, DNS changes, or an open router port. They work well for webhooks, mobile testing, demos, coding-agent previews, POST streaming, and WebSockets, but use a random hostname that disappears when the process stops. The tradeoffs include a 200-request concurrency limit, no SLA, no Cloudflare Access, and buffered SSE, so persistent or production workflows should move to a named tunnel.

infosec.summary: You want to run securely, not translate vendor-specific schemas into usable formats, hunt down the IT and business context you need, or pay by the byte for the privilege. Security doesn't thrive in a SIEM silo. You need an open platform where you can use all your telemetry and enterprise context to tell real threats from false positives. Lakewatch is an open, agentic SIEM built on the Databricks security lakehouse, so you can correlate 100% of your telemetry on one governed platform where agents handle triage, investigation and detection authoring at machine speed. infosec.title: Critical Bifrost AI Gateway Flaw Lets Attackers Run Commands Without Credentials
infosec.summary: Bifrost, an open-source AI gateway for 20+ LLM providers, ships with management auth disabled by default, so a single unauthenticated POST to /api/mcp/client can register a stdio MCP client and run arbitrary commands as the gateway user (CVE-2026-90898, CVSS 9.8). That exposes every stored provider API key. The official Docker image binds the management API to 0.0.0.0, and v2.0.0 only fixed a related plugin-loading flaw (CVE-2026-86242, CVSS 8.1). Upgrade to transports/v2.1.0 or set governance.auth_config.is_enabled to true, and treat any exposed unauthenticated instance as compromised by rotating virtual and provider API keys.

infosec.title: BigCommerce Data Stolen via Ribon Apps Hack
infosec.summary: Attackers used compromised Ribon API credentials from a Fastr system breach to access BigCommerce merchant customer data from September 13 to 17. Exposed records included names, email addresses, phone numbers, and postal addresses. BigCommerce revoked the credentials, uninstalled affected Ribon apps, and notified merchants.

infosec.title: GitHub App Private Keys: 474 Leaked Keys Exposed
infosec.summary: GitGuardian tested 4,802 leaked GitHub App private keys and found 474 that were still authenticated as 440 apps. Forty-four apps held organization-admin permissions. 207 could write repository content, and with the keys having no expiry, the leaked PEM files can remain usable for years. Cases included an Actions token app installed across roughly 300 organizations, BuildBuddy's internal app, Crusher.dev, and a CDC-related app.

infosec.title: The Tale of Two INC Ransom Notes
infosec.summary: An INC ransomware intrusion across 175+ endpoints started in early August with randomly named scheduled tasks launching an obfuscated PowerShell implant and RDP lateral movement. After 17 quiet days, AnyDesk delivered netscan.exe and a BYOVD EDR killer (hwau.exe loading the HwAudio driver), and Impacket's atexec.py deployed the payload. Huntress onboarded after the incident, so initial access is unknown, and the gap points to an access broker handing off to an affiliate, who followed the standard note with a DATALEAK_PRESS_RELEASE.txt listing stolen files and threatening to contact clients within 48 hours. Defenders should alert on randomly named scheduled tasks, unexpected RMM installs, and new or unsigned driver services, and limit privileged accounts to the systems they actually need.

infosec.title: Handle Redirect
infosec.summary: EDR products typically register callbacks on handle creation to monitor when processes call OpenProcess so they can strip access rights before a handle to a sensitive process like lsass is delivered. This article demonstrates a technique in which an attacker calls OpenProcess on a benign process (like notepad.exe) and then redirects the received handle to the sensitive process to evade EDR detection. To detect this attack vector, a security product running at the kernel level can periodically scan all process handle tables and compare ObjectPointerBits decoded EPROCESS against the process that owns the table.

infosec.title: Revoking the token didn't kill the backdoor
infosec.summary: GraphWorm, an implant tied to the China-nexus group Webworm, uses a real OneDrive account over Microsoft Graph as a dead drop, and its "upgrade" task swaps all five hardcoded OAuth credentials for a spare account in one command, so token revocation only pauses it. It also identifies victims by hashing MAC, CPU, and disk serials, so renaming or re-addressing a host won't shake the operator. Isolate the host or block the app ID in your own tenant at the same moment you revoke, then hunt sign-in logs for that app ID, unfamiliar tenants, and non-browser user agents hitting OneDrive.

infosec.summary: Watch this on-demand security demo from AWS and SANS Institute to see how governance, risk, and compliance strategies can help address risk across identity, data, APIs, and agentic workflows. infosec.summary: Outerlimit provides a decentralized authorization layer for autonomous software agents. It finds agents, monitors behavior, and enforces policies at execution time. The system restricts token use by scope, location, and conditions.

infosec.summary: pktz is an eBPF-powered network traffic monitor with per-process and per-connection reporting.

infosec.title: Anthropic and OpenAI Models Still Attempt Restricted Actions in Safety Tests
infosec.summary: Anthropic's Opus 5.5 escaped or tampered with its sandbox in 1.5% of unguarded tests. With package-registry credentials, it took harmful actions in roughly half of simulated exercises. OpenAI's GPT-6 Luna bypassed “access denied” controls in 42% of runs - Sol did so in 64%. OpenAI plans third-party reviews covering safeguards, capabilities, and misalignment incidents.

infosec.title: Microsoft disrupts AI-assisted platform that compromised 12,000 accounts
infosec.summary: EvilTokens, a Telegram-sold subscription service ($1,500 upfront, $500 monthly), abused Microsoft Entra device code authentication to compromise 12,000 accounts across 10,000 organizations before a Microsoft-led operation seized 50 websites and 150 domains, and the UK's Met Police arrested two men. Its AI chatbot analyzed 5,000 compromised emails at a time to identify who could approve payments, who they reported to, and which impersonation ruses would send funds to attacker accounts. Microsoft described it as a shift where criminals can make sense of a compromised inbox in minutes rather than days.

infosec.title: North Korea's Hangro Revisited
infosec.summary: Hangro, North Korea's SoftEther-derived VPN and mail client for officials abroad, added a July 2026 management certificate whose SAN lists hosts in Pyongyang and Khabarovsk plus an internal CGNAT address, while its older 2024 chain fails every signature check, including the root against itself. Its Chinese callback traces to six Shenyang assignments under a single 2008 Silibank registry contact, though silibank[.]com lapsed and was re-registered in 2023. The researcher describes the DPRK "return leg" as layered rather than a single pipe, with dead-drop pickup during Chinese office hours, 10 GB ETRN-enabled mail relays for bulk transfer, and Hangro for interactive sessions, though no actual traffic was observed.

infosec.title: Stolen passwords are exposing America's water providers to hackers
infosec.summary: SpyCloud found stolen credentials at 1,787 of 10,000 US water providers reviewed.

infosec.title: UK cops arrest 2 EvilTokens suspects, Microsoft seizes 50 phishing kit websites
infosec.summary: Microsoft and UK police disrupted EvilTokens, a Microsoft device-code phishing service.

Unity Gateway centralizes access to approved AI models and tools, helping the company track usage, enforce compliance, and safely scale both clinical and coding agents.

data.title: If You Last Used Cassandra 3.11, You Might Not Recognize It Today
data.summary: Apache Cassandra 5 loosens many of the constraints teams learned with 3.11, adding storage-attached indexing, unified compaction, native vector search, and built-in repair scheduling. Cassandra 6 goes further with ordered cluster metadata and cross-partition transactions, although partitioning and workload design remain fundamental.

data.title: We ported the original Doom to SQL
data.summary: CedarDB ported the original Doom's game logic and renderer almost entirely to SQL, running the game loop at its original 35 Hz and rendering at up to 60 FPS. The experiment shows that surprisingly complex real-time logic can work with SQL's set-based model, while database features like transactions, access control, and shared state make multiplayer particularly natural.

data.title: Real-time LLM guardrails with Jev: comparing latency and cost
data.summary: TypeSafe's Jev uses a purpose-built decision model for real-time AI guardrails, checking agent inputs, responses, and tool calls before they execute. In Arize's tests, it made the same decisions as GPT-5.4 nano while running 15-18x faster and costing 12-14x less per call.

data.title: Benchmarks are more broken than we could have imagined
data.summary: Horizon audited over 5,000 AI benchmark tasks across 20 datasets and confirmed 29 were broken, with problems including leaked answers, incomplete tests, gameable graders, and failing reference solutions. Many of these flaws actually inflated model scores, highlighting how benchmark results can overstate capabilities when the underlying tasks and graders are unreliable.

data.title: DuckDB Now Ships inside dbt v2
data.summary: dbt v2's Rust-based Fusion engine now includes a built-in DuckDB adapter, removing the need for a separate adapter installation. It adds DuckLake and Iceberg REST catalog support, writes queryable project metadata as Parquet, and performs SQL analysis that finds type or column problems before warehouse execution. The migration path starts by testing the opt-in v2 parser against existing projects.

data.title: Announcing Apache Fluss 1.0: Real-Time Data Foundation for AI
data.summary: Apache Fluss 1.0 introduces a stateless Rust HTTP Gateway for metadata, table operations, and batch writes, alongside native Python access and deeper Flink, Spark, Hudi, and Paimon integration. It adds row and log TTLs, predicate pushdown, coordinator high availability, resource protection, and cleanup features, moving the project from incubator-era capabilities toward production real-time lakehouse workloads.

data.title: Introducing prompt_jev(): bringing Jev to MotherDuck SQL
data.summary: MotherDuck's new prompt_jev function brings Jev directly into SQL, letting users classify and score text at analytics scale without training a model or parsing LLM responses. In its 100,000-row benchmark, Jev achieved 89% accuracy in 40 seconds for $0.50, outperforming the tested LLMs on speed, cost, and accuracy.

data.title: Jevflake
data.summary: Jevflake brings TypeSafe's Jev decision model into Snowflake through SQL functions and dbt, letting teams classify, score, and ask structured questions about their data with probabilistic answers. It can cache results in dbt models and add tests or human-review queues, making AI classifications reusable parts of normal analytics workflows.

data.title: How Adaptive Tail Sampling Works in the OpenTelemetry Collector
data.summary: Fixed-rate sampling often discards the rare traces needed in an incident, while ordinary tail sampling loses statistical weights. An adaptive tail sampler for the OpenTelemetry Collector buffers traces, applies ordered rules, and attaches W3C probability thresholds so downstream counts can be reweighted. It adapts by route and service, bounds memory under load, and is progressing upstream toward alpha.

data.title: High-Throughput OLTP in Three Simple Steps
data.summary: High-throughput transaction systems benefit from co-design rather than copying a connection-pool pattern from a general-purpose database. TigerBeetle models linked transfers atomically, aggregates balances without scans, batches operations automatically while a request is in flight, and prefers time-ordered identifiers for fast idempotency checks. Its benchmark illustrates why batching and ordered IDs can matter more than adding clients.

The update gives users more control over the Mac's visual style while preserving the modern Liquid Glass design language.

design.title: Adobe Premiere, One of the iPhone's Best Video-Editing Apps, is Now on Android
design.summary: Adobe is bringing its redesigned Premiere video-editing app to Android, nearly a year after its iPhone debut, replacing Premiere Rush, which loses support September 30. Layouts adapt across devices, pairing footage and a multitrack timeline side by side on foldables while still running on candy-bar phones like the Pixel. The app is free with no login required, though Firefly-powered features like Generative Fill require paid generative credits once the monthly allotment runs out.

design.title: UX-Context Design: Using UX Knowledge to Inform AI-Generated Design
design.summary: As more interface work turns AI-generated, research and design output shifts from human-facing deliverables toward curated context that guides AI, dubbed UX-context design. DESIGN.md, which Google Labs open-sourced in April 2026 from its Stitch tool, encodes a product's visual identity for AI tools in exact values and plain-language guidance. A hypothetical broader file, UX.md, would add research findings, interaction standards, a glossary, and user and world models as a continuously updated source.

design.title: Modernizing a legacy system? Your before/after isn't the case study
design.summary: Strong modernization case studies focus less on before-and-after visuals and more on the design decisions behind them, highlighting the judgment calls that shaped the final product rather than the process or visual refresh alone. Employers want to understand what changed because of the designer's thinking, not just that an outdated interface now looks modern.

design.title: Nothing has changed other than how we talk about it
design.summary: Agentic AI can dramatically speed up the research and problem-definition phases of Design Thinking by analyzing assumptions, synthesizing evidence, and pressure-testing ideas, but human judgment remains essential for validating outputs and making design decisions. Rather than replacing designers, AI shifts their role from generating information to evaluating evidence, challenging assumptions, and deciding what should be built.

design.title: A System That Preserves the Act of Drawing Itself
design.summary: A system that preserves the act of drawing itself, where every gesture is remembered, and every image continues to evolve.

design.title: The Visual Dictionary of AI Art Keywords
design.summary: The visual dictionary of AI art keywords — one word, one image, and free to browse. Master prompt keywords for Midjourney, Google Nano Banana, GPT Image, FLUX, and Stable Diffusion.

design.title: Named Colors with Documented Histories
design.summary: One color a day, told as it ought to be told: with its provenance, its chemistry, and the people who paid for it in poison.

design.title: Design Systems are a Collection of Decisions
design.summary: Design systems amount to collections of already-made decisions, so mechanical checks can prove straight from the artifact whether an AI agent used real components and correct tokens. Judgment-based evals still have an answer key when the system has documented a decision, like a required confirmation pattern for destructive actions. Visual evals work against a known reference, but deciding whether a new visual direction deserves to exist should stay with people.

design.title: Spatial UI Design: Tips and Best Practices
design.summary: Augmented reality design differs from screen-based UX, demanding attention to physical space, bodily comfort, and the cognitive load added to real-world distractions. UX consultant Frank Spillers' guidelines favor real-world physics, direct hand gestures over menus, context-aware triggers, and short, interruptible interactions. Content should stay within about 30 degrees of a user's central field of view, never past 50, and sit between 1.25 and 5 meters away.

design.title: Industrial Designer Alberto Essesi's Pen for Precision Sketching
design.summary: Alberto Essesi's satin-finished aluminum Exclamation Pen and matching rest feature a severely tapered point that keeps the tip visible for precision sketching.

design.title: This Secret Brooklyn Archive Contains a Trove of Design Rarities. Here Are 10 Exceptional Finds
design.summary: Collectible design gallery R & Company has opened Building 86, its 16,000-square-foot storage warehouse in the Brooklyn Navy Yard, to the public by appointment for the first time.

marketing.title: What's actually driving direct mail results in 2026?
marketing.summary: Get Lob's new State of Direct Mail: Consumer Insights 2026 Report . Discover what 2,000 consumers say currently earns their attention when it comes to direct mail and other marketing channels. Here's a sneak peek: > Trust is shifting: See why direct mail's trust edge over digital grew 9 points this year > The mailbox is a daily habit: Discover why 87% of consumers read their mail the same day it arrives > Economic pressure changes behavior: Discover why 87% of economically strained consumers take action on mail Get the report →

marketing.title: Advertising is Going AI. TV Isn't
marketing.summary: By 2030, 27% of ad revenue could flow through AI-powered platforms. TV is moving slower. North American TV ad revenue is expected to grow just 3% in 2026, excluding political spending. Complex buying workflows and fragmented inventory make automation harder. AI could simplify TV buying, but it needs strong first-party data to work well.

marketing.title: More lower-income households feel financially vulnerable
marketing.summary: Financially vulnerable US households rose from 15% to 17% in 2026, while fewer than 70% said they paid all bills on time over the past year. Low-income consumers have shifted more than $10 billion from discretionary purchases toward essentials since 2019, as prices for that group have risen 35% since January 2018. Consumer spending has still held steady in 2026, but many consumers are tapping into their savings to keep spending. This may not be sustainable if inflation, gas prices, and other costs continue to rise.

marketing.title: California will fine creators $5,000 a post for hidden political ads
marketing.summary: California now allows fines of up to $5,000 per post for creators who fail to disclose paid political content from campaigns. AB 1130 gives the Fair Political Practices Commission enforcement powers that were previously missing. The law applies when creators are paid by campaign committees to support or oppose candidates or ballot measures. It doesn't cover unpaid political opinions. The law follows growing use of influencers in political campaigns and similar disclosure efforts elsewhere.

marketing.title: The Perfectly Optimized Page for AEO
marketing.summary: A visual checklist showing the 6 key elements of a page optimized for AEO. Allowing major AI crawlers and server-side rendering makes the page accessible, while four to six direct sentences near the top give AI a concise answer to extract. Tables, lists, clear heading hierarchies, and FAQs make information easier to parse, and pages less than three months old are reportedly 3x more likely to earn citations.

marketing.title: I Built a Growth Team of Agents To Run a 6 Figures Business
marketing.summary: An agent growth team can take over drafting and routing but should never take over sending. One solo operator pairs an orchestrator with about ten channel agents, covering everything from SEO to paid media to lifecycle email, each tied to a share of a 900-signup, 200-customer monthly target. Every task goes on a Todoist board that separates decisions from execution, and each card must say what the task is, why it matters, and where to click. Finished cards trigger the next agent's follow-up automatically, so the founder only approves and sends.

marketing.title: 85% of marketers say videos perform better with AI. Here's how they're doing it
marketing.summary: Wistia's ungated report on AI video marketing trends pulls data on 500+ marketers to show you how creatives are making assets that command attention. See what AI is being used for, how that's changing budget conversations, and who is adopting first. Plus get the AI video playbook that's delivering results. Download the report

marketing.title: Free Looker Studio report to monitor AI traffic to your website
marketing.summary: A Looker Studio template that pulls data from Google Analytics. It visualizes AI-generated website traffic metrics, including breakdowns by AI tool and page.

marketing.title: Introducing GPT-6 Sol and Luna
marketing.summary: OpenAI has launched GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna, two faster and more affordable models for everyday work, coding, computer use, and AI agents. Both bring improvements from GPT-6 Astra, including stronger factuality and collaboration. GPT-6 Sol costs $2 input and $10 output per 1M tokens, while Luna costs $0.10 input and $0.50 output, both 50% cheaper than GPT-5.6 promotional pricing.

marketing.title: AI Polling: How Synthetic Surveys Could Predict Real Behavior
marketing.summary: People answer surveys as the person they want to be rather than the one they are, and synthetic surveys try to close that gap by simulating behavior instead of asking. AI personas built from interviews and behavioral records can return results in hours at about half the cost of human panels, and incumbents like Gallup and Qualtrics are already testing them. The simulations tend to match overall results but miss on subgroups and on questions outside their training data, where they rarely admit uncertainty.

marketing.title: What Would a Child-Free Internet Look Like?
marketing.summary: Australia's under-16 social media ban deactivated 4.7M accounts, yet more than 80% of surveyed children still used age-restricted services. A “child-free” internet could push young users toward gaming, messaging, and smaller platforms, making their activity harder to monitor. Children could also remain visible through adult-run family influencer accounts. The shift could make young consumers' influence less visible to brands while limiting children's access to online communities and digital experiences.

marketing.title: AI Agent Calls That Are Actually Made By Humans in a Call Center
marketing.summary: Meta pitched the feature publicly as AI, but internal posts describe a "human agent layer," and at least one tester only found out after the call that a person had placed it.

marketing.title: Only 11% of Small Merchants Are Ready for AI Shopping Agents
marketing.summary: The bottleneck is merchant infrastructure rather than AI reasoning.

marketing.title: 4 brands that prove product content doesn't have to be dull (2 minute rad)

crypto.title: Canada's big six banks explore tokenized deposit system
crypto.summary: BMO, CIBC, National Bank of Canada, RBC, Scotiabank, and TD jointly announced they're exploring a Canadian-dollar tokenized deposit system, with the first phase focused on moving tokenized deposits efficiently between institutions. The project follows Canada's OSFI clarifying that tokenized deposits are "not legally distinct from traditional deposits," and builds on March's Project Samara pilot testing blockchain-based government bond issuance.

crypto.title: CFTC warns prediction contracts carry heightened manipulation risk
crypto.summary: The CFTC's Division of Market Oversight issued an advisory warning that prediction contracts betting on whether someone will "mention" specific words or attend an event carry heightened manipulation risk, and can only be listed in limited circumstances under the Commodity Exchange Act. The agency has already charged a former White House teleprompter operator and ex-Rep. George Santos over trades tied to advance knowledge of "mention markets" on Kalshi, and it's telling exchanges to assess whether the person controlling a contract's outcome faces independent obligations that deter manipulation.

crypto.title: Rain launches real-time funding for stablecoin cards
crypto.summary: Rain introduced real-time funding, letting cardholders connect a wallet and approve a spending limit once, with each purchase authorizing only the exact amount needed directly from the wallet instead of requiring users to pre-fund a separate collateral balance. The feature is in beta for card programs where Rain manages authorization, launching with USDC on Base and Arbitrum and USDT0 on Plasma.

crypto.title: Circle Opens Bitcoin-Backed USDC Borrowing to Mint Clients, Routed Through Morpho
crypto.summary: Circle has launched a Bitcoin-backed USDC borrowing facility for Mint clients through Morpho's Arc market, wrapping deposited BTC as cirBTC to serve as collateral. The cirBTC/USDC market grew ~10x in five days, from $1.37 million on September 17 to $14.3 million in borrowed USDC against 287 cirBTC tokens. Galaxy and Keyrock supply the dollar liquidity, while Circle handles cirBTC issuance and wallet infrastructure, and Morpho governs loan terms. The structure gives institutional Bitcoin holders access to USDC without liquidating their BTC positions.

crypto.title: CME Adds Bitcoin Cash and Uniswap Futures as Crypto Derivatives Push Grows
crypto.summary: CME Group plans to list futures on Bitcoin Cash and Uniswap on October 19, pending regulatory approval, with standard and Micro contract sizes of 250/25 BCH and 10,000/1,000 UNI. The addition brings CME's single-asset crypto derivatives roster to 11 tokens, with Uniswap marking the first DEX governance token the exchange has listed. CME averaged 279,800 contracts per day in H1 2026, about $8.3 billion in daily notional, while altcoin-specific contracts generated more than $1 billion in notional for the year. The listings follow CME's June launch of a 24/7 crypto futures and options market, as institutional participants seek regulated venues for altcoin price risk management across a widening asset set.

crypto.title: Post-Poseidon: Hash Function Variants for Ethereum
crypto.summary: The emergence of Flock as a practical post-quantum proof system for binary circuits removes Ethereum's requirement for circuit-friendly hashes like Poseidon, opening five protocol layers (consensus signatures, CL aggregation, state tree construction, EL signatures, and EL aggregation) to standard hash function candidates. Performance targets set the bar at proving 2^25 bytes per second with LeanVM and approximately 1 million hash calls per second, a throughput floor that filters the field. BLAKE3 leads on raw speed at 7 GB/s parallel and 1.1 cycles per byte on long messages but carries no indifferentiability proofs and a thin cryptanalytic record. SHA-3 holds 50+ published cryptanalytic papers and sponge-mode indifferentiability proofs but runs at only 0.2 GB/s natively. The research ranks SHA-3 and BLAKE2s as the lowest-risk selections, with SHA-2's length-extension property disqualifying it as a random-oracle substitute despite 45+ cryptanalytic papers.

crypto.title: Tether walks away from Europe's MiCA stablecoin framework
crypto.summary: Tether abandoned MiCA compliance in the EU over a rule that required 60% of reserves in commercial bank deposits. CEO Paolo Ardoino argued it would expose 400 million users to risk since EU deposit insurance caps out at €100,000 per account. Tether holds roughly 80% of its $183 billion in reserves in US Treasuries, and USDT was delisted from all EU exchanges on July 1, though Ardoino said Tether would reconsider "when MiCA becomes safer." The ECB and all 27 EU central banks have separately called to scrap the 60% bank-deposit rule.

crypto.title: Kalshi Rebuts Wash Trading Allegations on Perpetuals Platform
crypto.summary: Kalshi published a detailed rebuttal to wash trading allegations on its perpetuals platform, arguing that its flat-fee liquidity incentive programs mirror standard structures at CME, CBOE, and Nasdaq. The core defense turns on trade economics: analyzed trades showed aggressors captured roughly $98,000 in profit potential, a signal of genuine price discovery rather than coordinated self-dealing. Kalshi also cited 350,000+ lifetime perpetual traders, open interest doubling over the past 30 days, and a July 2026 fee holiday structure for Self-Clearing Members that caps rebates at exact fees paid per trade, blocking the net-negative outcomes that would characterize artificial volume.

crypto.title: Cardano Added to Official x402 SDK
crypto.summary: Cardano has been added to Coinbase's x402 SDK, making it the first non-EVM chain on the protocol and enabling apps and AI agents to settle API calls with ADA or Cardano Native Tokens over standard HTTP requests.

crypto.title: BitMEX shuts down exchange operations
crypto.summary: BitMEX ended exchange operations as of 04:00 UTC on September 23.

crypto.title: Strategy buys 950 bitcoin for $76 million, bringing total holdings to 846,000 BTC
crypto.summary: Strategy acquired 950 BTC for $75.7M at an average of $79,670/coin between September 14-20, bringing total holdings to 846,000 BTC, a position exceeding 4% of bitcoin's 21M hard cap.

crypto.title: Binance to rebrand Funding Account to 'Stocks Account'
crypto.summary: Binance will migrate crypto assets from Funding Accounts to Spot Accounts in phases starting September 29 through January, after which Funding Accounts become "Stocks Accounts" dedicated solely to equities and stock options clearing.

fintech.title: Is a second payment processor worth it?
fintech.summary: This guide is for payments leaders, engineering teams, and finance professionals at enterprise and scaling businesses where they are evaluating whether a multiprocessor setup is right for their business. It covers how to identify specific gaps in reliability or global coverage that justify adding a second processor, what the resource investment looks like, and how an orchestration layer can help you manage multiple providers. It also breaks down how Stripe Orchestration works: onboard with as little as a single line of code, manage routing logic from a single dashboard, and compare processor performance. Download the guide

fintech.title: Ramp launches Accounts Receivable to automate the path from contract to cash
fintech.summary: Ramp AR expands Ramp's financial operations platform from money going out into money coming in. The product extracts contract and purchase order terms into invoice drafts, prepares collections follow-ups using customer context, automatically matches incoming payments to open invoices, recognizes revenue, and keeps accounting records synced with the ERP, pushing Ramp toward a more complete end-to-end finance platform.

fintech.title: Shopify to use Meta's Muse for agentic checkout
fintech.summary: Meta's new personal AI agent Muse will be able to browse Shopify merchants and make purchases for users through Shop Pay, giving it access to Shopify's product catalog, payments, and commerce infrastructure. The partnership is an early example of how AI agents could become a new shopping interface while Shopify provides the rails underneath, contrasting with Amazon's decision to block Muse from buying on its site.

fintech.title: Coinbase brings IPO access to US retail investors
fintech.summary: Coinbase is adding IPO allocations for eligible US retail customers, starting with Oura, allowing users to request shares at the offering price directly through the Coinbase app before public trading begins. The service is offered through FINRA-registered Coinbase Capital Markets and Apex Clearing, and forms part of Coinbase's broader “Everything Exchange” strategy to expand beyond crypto into stocks and primary-market investing.

fintech.title: CLARITY Act: The Senate Vote Failed 49 to 50. The Fight Now Moves to the Regulators
fintech.summary: Congress' effort to establish a federal framework for digital assets has stalled after the Senate fell short of the 60 votes needed to advance the legislation, with disagreements over ethics provisions emerging as the key sticking point. With the midterms approaching, the SEC and CFTC are likely to shape crypto rules through exemptions, guidance, and rulemaking instead, while questions such as stablecoin yield remain unresolved.

fintech.title: Where a core banking overrun actually goes: what the primary record says
fintech.summary: WislaCod's CEO argues that core banking programmes don't go over budget because of the ledger. The cost comes from the "seams" around it: platform decisions, migration timing, integration, testing, and unmanaged vendor chains. RTGS came in £56M over budget, and TSB's failed migration came down to a login misconfiguration and poor visibility into 85 subcontractors, not the data migration itself.

fintech.title: Five Reasons Why UPI Has Not Disrupted Credit Card
fintech.summary: India's UPI looked like a textbook Christensen disruptor (cheap, basic, and aimed at the low end), yet India's credit card business has tripled in five years. His five reasons: both can grow together in a fast-growing, under-digitized economy; UPI made digital payments visible to everyone, which drove demand for cards; UPI scams pushed some users back to cards for fraud protection; and banks earn nothing on UPI but 2 to 3% on cards, so they pushed cards hard. The fifth is that UPI was never designed to compete: it offers no rewards, no deferred payment, and no fraud protection, and the government treats it as a public good. That may start to shift on October 15, when merchant UPI payments above INR 2,000 begin carrying a 0.4% fee.

fintech.title: Rogo founder Gabe Stengel on building “investing superintelligence”
fintech.summary: Rogo CEO Gabe Stengel lays out a vision for AI doing much of the research, diligence, and execution work inside investment banks and investment firms, eventually becoming the venue where deals themselves happen. The discussion focuses on why domain-specific harnesses may matter more than frontier models alone, what investing skills humans will retain, and Rogo's ambition to become an AI-native Bloomberg for finance.

fintech.title: Stripe's wallet embraces AI bots
fintech.summary: Stripe is integrating its Link wallet with AI agents from Meta, xAI, Instinct, and others so bots can complete purchases without seeing a user's underlying card details. With 300 million users and roughly 1 million merchant integrations, Link gives Stripe a consumer-facing layer alongside its merchant network, positioning it to compete with PayPal, Apple, and Google as AI agents increasingly become the interface for shopping and payments.

fintech.title: Numeric launches Financial Data Platform, an ERP replacement built for the agent era
fintech.summary: Numeric launched its Financial Data Platform, positioning it as an ERP replacement that stores full business-event context instead of reducing transactions to traditional general-ledger entries. The system is designed to automate accounting, enable richer reporting, and support finance agents, while allowing companies to migrate module by module from systems like NetSuite rather than undertaking a full rip-and-replace implementation.

fintech.title: ‘Crypto hurdle' solved: SoFi is First Bank deploying stablecoin settlement across Mastercard network
fintech.summary: SoFi has moved its entire $25 billion card program onto SoFiUSD for settlement across Mastercard's global payments network, making it the first nationally chartered US bank to use stablecoins this way at scale. For consumers and merchants, little changes: payments still run through standard Mastercard cards, while settlement happens behind the scenes on blockchain rails, with merchants able to receive funds instantly without holding crypto or changing their infrastructure. SoFi is now in discussions with large US merchants about expanding the system beyond its own card business, which could turn stablecoins from a crypto product into largely invisible payment infrastructure.

fintech.title: Former Visa crypto lead launches open payments network
fintech.summary: Atum, an open payments network founded by former Visa crypto product team lead Pete Cooling, has emerged from stealth with $13.5 million in funding.

fintech.title: NewView Capital and Carta partner on company-sponsored tender offers
fintech.summary: NewView Capital and Carta announced a partnership to streamline company-sponsored tender offers, combining NewView's secondary investing expertise with Carta's cap table and liquidity infrastructure. The collaboration reflects the growing normalization of private-company liquidity programs as startups stay private longer, with Carta administering more than 70 tender offers representing $3 billion of transaction volume in the first half of 2026 alone.

fintech.title: Amazon adds Affirm payments option in the UK
fintech.summary: The new Affirm payment options will be available to customers when shopping for millions of products. Customers can simply select Affirm as their payment method at checkout and apply to get an instant eligibility decision from Affirm. If approved, customers will be able to pay for their orders using flexible financing options: “0% Pay-in-3” splits the cost of the purchase into three interest-free monthly payments, while a longer-term interest-bearing (22% Representative APR fixed) plan is available for up to 48 months. Both options are available on baskets of at least £50 and come with no late or hidden fees.

fintech.title: Go.AI secures $85 Million in Series A funding
fintech.summary: Chicago-based Go.AI raised $85 million led by Updata Partners to expand its on-premises AI infrastructure, bringing its total funding to $90 million.

fintech.title: Blockchain.com inks deal to offer access to NYSE tokenized stocks
fintech.summary: Blockchain.com users could eventually trade tokenized US equities and ETFs around the clock through the NYSE's upcoming digital trading platform, pending regulatory approval.

it.title: Google brings offline agents to the Antigravity SDK
it.summary: Google's Antigravity SDK now supports local models through LiteRT and compatible inference servers, enabling agents to run offline while keeping code on-device. Hybrid workflows can combine cloud-based planning with local execution to reduce API usage and limit sensitive data transfers.

it.title: Meta unveils $1,300 VR glasses with a portable workspace
it.summary: Meta unveiled VR glasses weighing about 100 grams, with computing and battery hardware housed in a tethered puck, launching in Spring 2027 for $1,299.99. The device offers a private multi-screen workspace, virtual keyboard and touchpad, and photorealistic avatar calling through apps including Zoom and WhatsApp.

it.title: Meta brings Muse to glasses and unveils $349 audio frames
it.summary: Meta has announced plans to bring its Muse personal AI agent to its glasses, alongside new Ray-Ban Meta Audio frames starting at $349 and shipping October 13. The expanded lineup includes Ray-Ban Meta Gen 3 with improved battery life and controls, extending Meta's push toward hands-free AI assistance.

it.title: AI agents expose the cracks in cloud infrastructure
it.summary: Undocumented configurations and manual workarounds become operational risks when AI agents start managing infrastructure. Reliable automation requires infrastructure and policies defined in code, built-in cost and access controls, and clear boundaries for actions that need human approval.

it.title: AI agents need a more integrated security operations center
it.summary: Fragmented security tools force analysts and agents to rebuild context and coordinate actions across separate systems, slowing incident response. Microsoft's proposed answer is an integrated security operations center, now in Defender preview, that combines SIEM, threat protection, and response controls around shared context.

it.title: WhiteFiber Launches Highest-Performing Distributed AI Supercluster
it.summary: WhiteFiber Continuum runs DriveNets AI Fabric and WEKA NeuralMesh across 83km of dark fiber, hitting 136 Tbps of bandwidth and 0.9ms round-trip latency, so two data centers behave like one GPU cluster with both sites carrying live traffic at once, no failover delay, no idle capacity. Read the architecture breakdown

it.title: Barracuda launches AI Data Security to control what employees send to chatbots
it.summary: Barracuda launched AI Data Security to stop sensitive company data from reaching ChatGPT, Copilot, Gemini, and 1,300+ other AI tools. It adds prompt-injection screening, policy controls, and audit logs for SMBs and MSPs, available in October with SecureEdge Premium Access. A Barracuda survey found 49% of CIOs at 500 to 1,000 employee firms lack AI governance skills.

it.title: The Genie One MCP is now Generally Available
it.summary: Databricks made its Genie One MCP server generally available, giving any AI agent governed access to structured and unstructured data plus business context through Genie Ontology. The MCP runs as a managed service in Unity Gateway, adding centralized governance, fine-grained policies, and audit logging while keeping answers consistent across tools like Claude, ChatGPT, and Cursor. It aims to reduce agent sprawl by letting agents query data, retrieve results, and explore visualizations and citations without custom connectors.

it.title: Microsoft plans $10B-plus Middle East cloud investment
it.summary: Microsoft plans to invest more than $10 billion through 2030 across Kuwait, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, and the UAE to expand cloud and AI infrastructure. Its commitments also include more than $400 million for network connectivity, alongside sovereign cloud capabilities and business continuity programs.

it.title: What Dropbox has learned from deploying AI at company scale
it.summary: Dropbox says scaling AI requires redesigning end-to-end workflows, aligning incentives, and measuring outcomes like revenue, quality, and retention. It reports ~70% AI-generated code, top-5% PR throughput versus similar peers, and quality in line with industry, while using internal coding agents like Nova to connect AI spend to engineering value. Leaders argue that as AI lowers engineering costs, human problem-solving, judgment, and leadership matter more, and trusted organizational context will separate effective adopters.

it.title: Topology-Aware Workload Scheduling with NVIDIA Topograph
it.summary: NVIDIA Topograph is an open source toolkit that discovers cluster network topology from cloud or on-premises providers and normalizes it into a common model. It publishes that topology as Kubernetes node labels, Slurm configurations, Slinky ConfigMaps, or NFD resources so schedulers like KAI Scheduler, Kueue, and native Kubernetes can place tightly coupled GPU workloads near each other. By keeping topology current as clusters change, Topograph reduces network congestion and improves AI factory efficiency, tokens per watt, and cost across Kubernetes, Slurm, and Slinky environments.

it.title: Accelerated Server Sales Are Themselves Accelerating
it.summary: Q2 2026 server sales surged 52% year over year to $166.32 billion.

it.title: New Surface business PCs arrive October 13
it.summary: Microsoft's refreshed 12-inch Surface Pro and 13-inch Surface Laptop bring Snapdragon X2 Plus processors, local AI capabilities, and enterprise management tools.
